title: The local generic fibre is the pullback of the boundary open
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme and $c:C\to S$ any morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $U\subseteq S$ be open, and $s\notin U$ such that every generalization $t$ of $s$ outside $U$ equals $s$. Suppose $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is a discrete valuation ring, meaning a local principal ideal domain which is not a field. Write $K=k(S)$ [def-sc-function-field], $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$, $L=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}A$, $d:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $g:L\to C$, $b:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $L_K=L\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with projection $p:L_K\to L$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $k:L_K\to C_U$ satisfies $k i_U=p g$, then the square $(k,p,i_U,g)$ is cartesian. No hypothesis on smoothness or quasi-compactness of $c$ is needed.

proof.text: Choose an irreducible uniformizer pi of A=O_{S,s}. Every nonzero element is associated to a power of pi by associated_pow_irreducible. The function field K of S is a fraction field of A; iff_of_le_of_exists_dvd then makes K a localization away from pi. Hence Spec K to Spec A is an open immersion with image D(pi).

The span of pi is the maximal ideal. A prime contains pi exactly when it is the closed point, by maximality and properness. The map Spec A to S is injective and sends its closed point to s. Minimality says all the other points map into U. Thus the inverse image of U is D(pi), the image of Spec K.

Pulling back the open immersion Spec K to Spec A makes L_K to L an open immersion. Its opensRange is the inverse image of D(pi) under L to Spec A. By the pullback condition this is the inverse image of C_U under L to C. The square specified by k and hk is cartesian by IsOpenImmersion.isPullback. Empty total spaces need no separate hypothesis.
